scope: Append-only quantitative holdouts found in the final Africa/Middle East evidence pass. These records improve physical-yield and archaeological-demography validation, but none is promoted to a global scale anchor: each lacks a complete, independently demonstrated Malthusian saturation interval and/or a closed EU5 boundary.

promotion_audit.decision: No new training target is admitted. Rasulid Ta'izz supplies a dated, source-backed cereal-yield test; the Fayyum register supplies village-level fiscal/water/yield fields but only a partial poll-tax count; Jenné-jeno supplies a quantitative archaeological settlement-population interval, but it is out of period and is a validation-only analogue. None may be converted into a population-capacity target by an assumed tax, household or density multiplier.
promotion_audit.review_method: Independent source review checked the date, population semantics, local-food evidence, pressure/saturation evidence, shock and trade confounding, source-family independence, boundary definition and EU5 crosswalk status. Quantities are retained only with their original semantics and uncertainty.

records.label: Rasulid Ta'izz cereal yields in the 692/1293 crop register
records.interval_semantics: This is a physical crop-yield holdout, not a population observation. The register gives gross grain harvested per seed measure on best, medium and poor land. Seed, processing, storage, feed, fallow, dietary and risk deductions have not been applied; those remain model calculations.
quantitative_evidence: Varisco, 'Pars Pro Toto Observation: Historical Anthropology in the Textual Field of Rasulid Yemen' (2006), pp. 161-174, reports the royal register and identifies the 692/1293 Ta'izz cereal entries.

The Ta'izz zabad/azbud is a capacity measure rather than a mass unit. Varisco's discussion gives approximately 8.9 Egyptian ratl and about 450 g per ratl, or roughly 4 kg per Ta'izz measure; the unit conversion is uncertain and is therefore kept separate from the ratio test.
The ratios are gross harvest-to-seed ratios. They are used to test crop-date, water-mode and yield-unit semantics only; no people-support estimate is derived from them.
pressure_evidence: The register distinguishes best, medium and poor land and records production assessment across the Ta'izz district, providing a dated test of heterogeneous low-input cereal productivity.
It does not establish that Ta'izz was at a long-run Malthusian equilibrium, nor does it give a complete population, food-balance or saturation interval.
shock_flags: gross yield rather than edible net calories
historical district polygon not yet closed to EU5
records.trade_dependence: unresolved for the Ta'izz district; do not use port/customs evidence as local food support
records.food_regime: low-input wheat, emmer and barley with highland/irrigated Yemen agriculture
records.boundary_description: Ta'izz fiscal/crop district represented by the 692/1293 entries; the register's district extent is not a closed geospatial polygon equivalent to an EU5 location or province.
records.boundary_source: Varisco (2006), pp. 161-174; Varisco (1991), Journal of the Economic and Social History of the Orient 34:1-22
records.source_family_independence: independent dated agricultural-register evidence; same broader Rasulid bundle as the existing Yemen tax record, so it does not add an independent population anchor family
missing_criteria: population or capacity interval for the same Ta'izz boundary
closed historical district polygon and >=95% EU5 crosswalk
validated unit conversion and net-calorie accounting
records.notes: Use as a crop-physics regression fixture. A valid implementation must preserve the land-quality ordering and must not infer irrigated yield by copying the rain-fed value or infer population from the tax register.

records.label: Fayyum al-Nabulusi 1245 village tax, crop and water-right matrix
records.interval_semantics: This is a village-level fiscal and food-system holdout. The database contains 124 settlement rows with crop/tax, water-right and village-institution fields. Poll-tax heads are partial taxable non-Muslim adult counts, not total population, and tax in kind is an assessment rather than a calorie total.

quantitative_evidence.coverage_note: all rows in the downloadable village register
fiscal entries only; not a complete regional production total
partial non-Muslim/adult head counts; explicitly not total population or a lower bound on all inhabitants

pressure_evidence: The register records crop levies, canal/water rights, village maintenance and agricultural institutions, supplying local production and water-management features.
Water stress and canal maintenance are production-pressure indicators, but no independent saturation fraction or complete household/population total is established for the same 124-village boundary.
shock_flags: poll tax excludes Muslims and non-taxable demographic groups
tax/levy quantities are fiscal assessments, not net edible calories
settlement and canal map is a point/grid reconstruction rather than a closed aggregate polygon
Fayyum/Cairo redistribution and trade dependence unresolved
records.trade_dependence: local Nile agriculture is documented, but the Fayyum food-budget import/export share is unresolved
records.food_regime: Nile irrigation with cereals, legumes, rice, sugar cane, livestock and village gardens
records.boundary_description: The 124 villages/hamlets in the al-Nabulusi register and their canal/water-right entries; the project map identifies settlements by a historical grid, but a complete polygon and EU5 intersection remain unresolved.
records.boundary_source: Queen Mary Rural Society in Medieval Islam database, village register, settlement table and Fayyum map
records.boundary_confidence: medium for village/grid points; low for complete aggregate polygon
records.source_family_independence: independent edited primary-register/database family; not a complete population census
missing_criteria: complete population interval for the 124-village boundary
closed historical polygon and >=95% EU5 crosswalk
conversion from fiscal levies to net local-food calories
records.notes: This matrix should be used to test water-access, crop-family and fiscal-yield feature lineage. The 1,142 poll-tax heads must remain explicitly partial and must never be multiplied into a total population label.

records.label: Jenné-jeno and satellite-tell constellation, Inland Niger Delta
records.interval_semantics: Validation-only archaeological settlement-population interval, not a 1337 capacity target. McIntosh and McIntosh report approximately 7,000-13,000 for a core/satellite interpretation; Monroe reports approximately 10,000-27,000 for the wider constellation of tell sites. The deliberately wide 7,000-27,000 interval preserves the published definition and method disagreement. No saturation fraction is inferred.
quantitative_evidence: McIntosh and McIntosh (1981), Journal of African History 22:1-22, report a >33 ha Jenne-Jeno site, a survey of about 1,100 km2 and a high-density rural settlement system; their settlement estimates include approximately 7,000-13,000 people for the core/satellite interpretation.

Monroe (2018), Journal of Archaeological Research 26:337-377, DOI 10.1007/s10814-017-9114-2, describes systematic survey of about 1,100 km2, more than 400 tell sites and approximately 10,000-27,000 people in the mid/late first-millennium constellation.

The site and satellite settlements were sustained by local rice, fish/fish oil, cattle and wild foods, with craft and interregional exchange; the local-food share is not numerically resolved, so it is not used as a saturation target.
pressure_evidence: Settlement density peaked around AD 700-1100, with a documented decline after roughly AD 1150 and substantial abandonment/relocation by AD 1200-1400.

The density peak and later abandonment are useful stress/trajectory diagnostics, but they do not prove a Malthusian equilibrium: political reorganization, trade shifts and relocation are unresolved confounders.
shock_flags: archaeological population estimates depend on settlement definition and chronology
mixed local subsistence and interregional trade
historical tell-concentration polygon not yet intersected with EU5 geometry
records.trade_dependence: mixed; local rice/fish/cattle/wild foods documented, but craft and interregional exchange are also documented
records.food_regime: Inland Niger Delta floodplain rice, fish/fish oil, cattle and wild foods
records.boundary_description: The Jenné-jeno tell and satellite-tell constellation within approximately 1 km of the archaeological site at 13.88977 N, -4.54072 W; the circle is a locator geometry for validation and is not a claim that the surrounding EU5 province had the same population.
records.boundary_source: McIntosh & McIntosh (1981); Monroe (2018); archaeological site coordinates from the site locator
records.boundary_confidence: medium for archaeological site/constellation locator; low for EU5 area coverage
records.source_family_independence: independent archaeological survey/demographic-reconstruction family; out-of-period and not a capacity anchor
missing_criteria: 1337-compatible date and technology for scale supervision
independent saturation fraction or carrying-capacity interval
closed historical constellation polygon and audited >=95% EU5 crosswalk
records.notes: This is the strongest newly found quantitative African validation case, not a training target. A model that predicts an implausibly low capacity for the local floodplain should fail a diagnostic, but the archaeological population interval cannot be used to force a global scale or a surrounding-land multiplier.
